arxiv-2105-07514.title: The Cluster Depth Tests: Toward Point-Wise Strong Control of the Family-Wise Error Rate in Massively Univariate Tests with Application to M/EEG
arxiv-2105-07514.creator: Jaromil Frossard, Olivier Renaud
arxiv-2105-07514.description: Abstract The cluster mass test has been widely used for massively univariate tests in M/EEG, fMRI and, recently, pupillometry analysis. It is a powerful method for detecting effects while controlling weakly the family-wise error rate (FWER), although its correct interpretation can only be performed at the cluster level without any point-wise conclusion.

arxiv-2201-05173.title: The Combinatorics of Salva Veritate Principles
arxiv-2201-05173.creator: Norman E. Trushaev
arxiv-2201-05173.description: Abstract Various concepts of grammatical compositionality arise in many theories of both natural and artificial languages, and often play a key role in accounts of the syntax-semantics interface. We propose that many instances of compositionality should entail non-trivial combinatorial claims about the expressive power of languages which satisfy these compositional properties.

arxiv-2210-03515.title: Spiking Neural Networks for Nonlinear Regression
arxiv-2210-03515.creator: Alexander Henkes, Jason K. Eshraghian, Henning Wessels
arxiv-2210-03515.description: Abstract Spiking neural networks, also often referred to as the third generation of neural networks, carry the potential for a massive reduction in memory and energy consumption over traditional, second-generation neural networks. Inspired by the undisputed efficiency of the human brain, they introduce temporal and neuronal sparsity, which can be exploited by next-generation neuromorphic hardware.

arxiv-2304-08743.title: Benchmarking Actor-Critic Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Robotics Control with Action Constraints
arxiv-2304-08743.creator: Kazumi Kasaura, Shuwa Miura, Tadashi Kozuno, Ryo Yonetani, Kenta Hoshino, Yohei Hosoe
arxiv-2304-08743.description: Abstract This study presents a benchmark for evaluating action-constrained reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms. In action-constrained RL, each action taken by the learning system must comply with certain constraints. These constraints are crucial for ensuring the feasibility and safety of actions in real-world systems.

arxiv-2305-09316.title: Enhancing Keyphrase Extraction from Long Scientific Documents using Graph Embeddings
arxiv-2305-09316.creator: Roberto Martínez-Cruz, Debanjan Mahata, Alvaro J. López-López, José Portela
arxiv-2305-09316.description: Abstract In this study, we investigate using graph neural network (GNN) representations to enhance contextualized representations of pre-trained language models (PLMs) for keyphrase extraction from lengthy documents. We show that augmenting a PLM with graph embeddings provides a more comprehensive semantic understanding of words in a document, particularly for long documents.

arxiv-2310-16079.title: The Magic Renormalisability of Affine Gaudin Models
arxiv-2310-16079.creator: Falk Hassler, Sylvain Lacroix, Benoît Vicedo
arxiv-2310-16079.description: Abstract We study the renormalisation of a large class of integrable σ \sigma -models obtained in the framework of affine Gaudin models. They are characterised by a simple Lie algebra 𝔤 \mathfrak{g} and a rational twist function φ ⁡ ( z ) \varphi(z) with simple zeros, a double pole at infinity but otherwise no further restrictions on the pole structure.

arxiv-2404-07165.title: Pressure-tuned many-body phases through 𝚪 {\bf\Gamma} -K valleytronics in moiré bilayer WSe 2
arxiv-2404-07165.creator: Marta Brzezińska, Sergii Grytsiuk, Malte Rösner, Marco Gibertini, Louk Rademaker
arxiv-2404-07165.description: Abstract Recent experiments in twisted bilayer transition-metal dichalcogenides have revealed a variety of strongly correlated phenomena. To theoretically explore their origin, we combine here ab initio calculations with correlated model approaches to describe and study many-body effects in twisted bilayer WSe 2 under pressure.

arxiv-2406-06762.title: Ricci curvature bounds and rigidity for non-smooth Riemannian and semi-Riemannian metrics
arxiv-2406-06762.creator: Michael Kunzinger
arxiv-2406-06762.description: Abstract We study rigidity problems for Riemannian and semi-Riemannian manifolds with metrics of low regularity. Specifically, we prove a version of the Cheeger-Gromoll splitting theorem [ 22 ] for Riemannian metrics and the flatness criterion for semi-Riemannian metrics of regularity C 1 C^{1} .

arxiv-2506-19828.title: High-Efficiency Tunable Microwave Photon Detector Based on a Semiconductor Double Quantum Dot Coupled to a Superconducting High-Impedance Cavity
arxiv-2506-19828.creator: Fabian Oppliger, Wonjin Jang, Aldo Tarascio, Franco De Palma, Christian Reichl, Werner Wegscheider, Ville F. Maisi, Dominik Zumbühl, Pasquale Scarlino
arxiv-2506-19828.description: Abstract High-efficiency single-photon detection in the microwave domain is a key enabling technology for quantum sensing, communication, and information processing. However, the extremely low energy of microwave photons ( ∼ μ \sim\mu eV) presents a fundamental challenge, preventing direct photon-to-charge conversion as achieved in optical systems using semiconductors.

pmc-10552393.title: Injectable biocompatible nanocomposites of Prussian blue nanoparticles and bacterial cellulose as a safe and effective photothermal cancer therapy
pmc-10552393.creator: Hwichan Hong, MinKyu Kim, Wooseung Lee, Miyeon Jeon, Chaedong Lee, Hoonsub Kim, Hyung-Jun Im, Yuanzhe Piao
pmc-10552393.description: Photothermal therapy (PTT) is a novel cancer treatment using a photoabsorber to cause hyperthermia to kill tumors by laser irradiation. Prussian blue nanoparticles (PB NPs) are considered as next-generation photothermal agents due to the facile synthesis and excellent absorption of near-infrared light. Although PB NPs demonstrate remarkable PTT capabilities, their clinical application is limited due to their systemic toxicity.

pmc-10636093.title: Improving explainable AI with patch perturbation-based evaluation pipeline: a COVID-19 X-ray image analysis case study
pmc-10636093.creator: Jimin Sun, Wenqi Shi, Felipe O. Giuste, Yog S. Vaghani, Lingzi Tang, May D. Wang
pmc-10636093.description: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have sparked interest in developing explainable AI (XAI) methods for clinical decision support systems, especially in translational research. Although using XAI methods may enhance trust in black-box models, evaluating their effectiveness has been challenging, primarily due to the absence of human (expert) intervention, additional annotations, and automated strategies.

pmc-10822946.title: Why do democracies respond differently to COVID-19? A comparison of the United States and South Korea
pmc-10822946.creator: Yexin Mao
pmc-10822946.description: BackgroundCOVID-19 has posed severe challenges to crisis management in democracies. Different democracies respond to the crisis differently. This article proposes an analytical framework to explain why democracies respond differently to the public health crisis and how different contextual factors affect crisis response in democracies.

pmc-11451523.title: Aridity drives the response of soil total and particulate organic carbon to drought in temperate grasslands and shrublands
pmc-11451523.creator: Baoku Shi, Manuel Delgado-Baquerizo, Alan K. Knapp, Melinda D. Smith, Sasha Reed, Brooke Osborne, Yolima Carrillo, Fernando T. Maestre, Yu Zhu, Anping Chen, Kate Wilkins, Martin C. Holdrege, Andrew Kulmatiski, Catherine Picon-Cochard, Christiane Roscher, Sally Power, Kerry M. Byrne, Amber C. Churchi
pmc-11451523.description: The increasing prevalence of drought events in grasslands and shrublands worldwide potentially has impacts on soil organic carbon (SOC). We leveraged the International Drought Experiment to study how SOC, including particulate organic carbon (POC) and mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC) concentrations, responds to extreme drought treatments (1-in-100-year) for 1 to 5 years at 19 sites worldwide.

pmc-12714694.title: Comparative TSS-seq analysis among natural variations of Arabidopsis reveals the genetic stability of genic and nongenic promoters
pmc-12714694.creator: Kazuki Sugekawa, Okechukwu S Ezeh, Yoshiharu Y Yamamoto
pmc-12714694.description: In a previous TSS-seq analysis, we identified >300 K promoters in the Arabidopsis genome. The majority were nongenic promoters, composed of intragenic, antisense, and orphan promoters. Although several nongenic promoters for biological processes have been identified, the significance of these nongenic promoters is unclear.

pmc-12821703.title: Applying Principles of Biomechanics of the Spine to Martial Arts: A Review on Balance of Stances in Goju-Ryu Karate-Do
pmc-12821703.creator: Michael Fiechter, Tobias Pötzel, Marc E. Pfeifer
pmc-12821703.description: Balance is referred to as a state of equilibrium where forces of agonist and antagonistic muscles are equal. This is particularly relevant in the practice of Goju-Ryu Karate-Do, a martial art style with combinations of hard and soft techniques. Particularly, karate stances not only depend on technical aspects but also on the ability to achieve a centered posture.

pmc-13342111.title: Astrocytic ankyrin-2 enables memory persistence in the mouse hippocampus
pmc-13342111.creator: Hayoung Kim, Jiwoon Lim, Jooyoung Kim, Erva Ozkan, Gyu Hyun Kim, HyoJin Park, Mingu Gordon Park, Bitna Joo, Sangkyu Lee, Kea Joo Lee, Bong-Kiun Kaang, C Justin Lee, Wuhyun Koh
pmc-13342111.description: Memory persistence, the ability to retain information over time, is a fundamental feature of long-term memory. Although astrocytes contribute to synaptic plasticity, the molecular mechanisms by which they support memory persistence remain unclear. Here we show that astrocytic ankyrin-2 (Ank2) is required for memory persistence in adult mice.

pmc-13458867.title: Optimizing Laboratory Autoverification in Complete Blood Count Testing Using Machine Learning: A Performance Evaluation Study
pmc-13458867.creator: Sinsorn Srirujee, Peempol Chokchaipermpoonphol
pmc-13458867.description: BackgroundAutoverification improves laboratory efficiency by reducing manual reviews; however, rule‐based systems may lack flexibility, particularly in complete blood count (CBC) testing. Machine learning (ML) can potentially enhance performance by recognizing complex patterns in laboratory data. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate ML‐based autoverification systems in classifying CBC results compared to traditional rule‐based methods.
